title: Loops
examples: When should I use a for loop instead of a while loop?
What happens if I forget to update the counter in a while loop?

explain.say: Today we are learning about loops in coding.

items: They save you from writing the same code many times.

explain.say: A for loop is great when you know how many times to repeat.
The syntax usually involves a starting number, an ending number, and a step.

items: Start Value | End Value | Step Value

explain.say: A while loop repeats as long as a certain condition stays true.
For example, we can use a loop to count up to ten.
In real life, think about turning on a set of lights.

faq.q: How do I know which loop to use?
faq.a: Use a for loop when you know the exact number of times you need to repeat something. You might also use a while loop if the repetition depends on something changing.
asks: Should I use for or while?
When is a for loop better?

faq.q: What is the most important thing to remember in a while loop?
faq.a: You must make sure that something inside the loop eventually changes so the condition becomes false. Otherwise, the loop will run forever, which is called an infinite loop.
asks: How do I stop a while loop?

faq.q: Can I use loops to count backwards?
faq.a: Yes, you can set your loop's step value to a negative number. This tells the loop to count down instead of up.
asks: How to count down in a loop?
Does the step value have to be positive?

faq.q: What if I use a for loop but the condition is never met?
faq.a: If the starting value is already greater than the ending value, the loop will simply not run at all. This is perfectly fine.
asks: Will the loop run zero times?

faq.q: Are loops only for counting numbers?
faq.a: No, loops can repeat any action, like printing text or checking if a user entered a correct password. The action does not have to be a number.
asks: Can loops do things other than count?

facts: A loop executes a block of code multiple times.
For loops are best when the number of repetitions is known beforehand.
While loops continue executing as long as a specified condition remains true.
It is crucial to update a variable inside a while loop to prevent infinite looping.

quiz.say: If a for loop runs from 0 to 3, how many times does the code inside run?
quiz.why: The loop includes both the start and end numbers, so it runs for 0, 1, 2, and 3.

wrong.1: This is a common mistake because students sometimes forget to count the starting number.
wrong.2: This happens if you only count the steps between the start and end numbers.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you only count the last number in the sequence.

quiz.say: A while loop checks a condition before running code. If the condition is false initially, what happens?

options.show: It runs until the condition becomes false.
options.say: It runs until the condition becomes false.

quiz.why: The loop checks the condition first, and if it is false, it skips the code block entirely.

wrong.0: This suggests the loop will run at least once, which is not guaranteed.
wrong.1: While it stops, it does not necessarily cause a program error.
wrong.3: This mistake assumes the check itself counts as one run.

quiz.say: To count down from 10 to 1, which loop structure is most appropriate?

options.show: For loop with a negative step
options.say: For loop with a negative step

options.show: For loop with a positive step
options.say: For loop with a positive step

quiz.why: A for loop allows you to explicitly set a negative step value to count downwards accurately.

wrong.0: While loops can do it, the for loop is designed for this type of fixed iteration.
wrong.2: While this works, a for loop is often cleaner for fixed count ranges.
wrong.3: Using a positive step will cause the loop to count up, not down.
